content:
Sofia L.: Heads-up: deployed the keystore principal scoping change to staging ~5m ago. Seeing mTLS handshake failures for eu-west ingest services. Anyone else?
Jamal R.: saw a spike in TLS failures around the same time. quick log: \u003ctimestamp\u003e tls: handshake error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
Elaine (oncall): grabbing logs now. can you paste the audit deny entry if any?
Sofia L.: here — audit log from edge-proxy: 
```
audit: kms.Decrypt DENY principal=service-account:platform-keystore-scoped reason=iam:condition_eval_failed resource=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/keystore
```
Patrick M.: that smells like the RBAC condition tightened principal scope and the keystore SA lost iam:decrypt in the eu-west binding. Did the scoping patch change the principal name?
Sofia L.: yes, we changed bound principal from `service-account:platform-keystore@infra` -> `service-account:platform-keystore@infra:scoped-eu` (annotation-driven). The keystore binder should have added the new binding but looks like it didn't for eu-west.
Maria G.: quick mitigation: rollback RBAC change for eu-west while we root cause. I've queued a rollback canary. deploy-bot: rollback queued for staging keystore-scope v2 -> v1. ETA ~3m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
sec-bot: flagging incident:INC-2026-172 - mtls-handshake-eu-west-keystore. Notified incident channel.
Elaine (oncall): forensics — run `openssl s_client -connect ingest-eu-west.internal:443 -servername ingest-eu-west.internal -showcerts` and check issuer chain. Also check proxy SNI mapping; sometimes SNI mismatch causes trusted bundle to be different.
Jamal R.: ran openssl; server cert chain shows intermediate signed by our internal CA, but client certs are being rejected. Error in the proxy: `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate`
Patrick M.: that aligns with KMS decrypt deny — the proxy can't unwrap client cert private key? or the keystore failed to return the intermediate chain. Check keystore logs: `kubectl -n infra logs keystore-...`
Sofia L.: keystore logs show repeated `KMS.Decrypt DENY` with condition string: `request.region == us && request.binding == legacy`. Our condition is too restrictive for eu-west.
Maria G.: action items: 1) revert scoping for eu-west (in flight), 2) update keystore binder to write a region-scoped binding for `eu-west`, 3) add audit rule to alert when KMS returns DENY with mtls in last 10s.
Elaine (oncall): I also want a short-term bypass: allow the keystore pod identity to perform decrypt using the broader principal (temporarily) so handshakes succeed. We need a JIT change with an expiration.
Jamal R.: agree. I'll push a patch granting `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` to `service-account:platform-keystore@infra` in the eu-west project for 1 hour. Patch command: 
```
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-eu-west \
  --member=serviceAccount:platform-keystore@infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter \
  --condition='title=temporary-keystore-eu,expression=timestamp("2026-03-21T12:30:00Z") > request.time' 
```
(we'll tighten the condition properly later)
Patrick M.: also check that the keystore is returning correct trust bundle. Run: `curl -s http://keystore.internal/ca-bundle | sha256sum` on staging/eu-west and compare to us-west.
Sofia L.: did that: eu-west sha256 `a1b2...3f`, us-west `a1b2...3f` — identical bundle. So trust bundle is fine; it's KMS decrypt DENY.
Maria G.: long-term fix: we need to unify the principal naming scheme in the binder. The change to append region scoping broke IAM conditions. The binder should populate both global and region-limited principals until rollout completes.
Elaine (oncall): for the incident timeline: record the RBAC change commit hash, time, and who approved. Add to incident doc. Linking playbook: https://redwood.internal/docs/security/mtls-handshake-playbook (internal).
Jamal R.: also found a subtlety: our RBAC condition uses `request.region` label which is absent in some KMS audit contexts. When absent, condition eval = false -> DENY. Need to fallback to `global` if region label missing.
Patrick M.: ok I'll open a binder PR to add fallback logic and a unit test that simulates missing request labels.
sec-bot: automated note: added `kms.decrypt.deny` alert to sec-telemetry channel for 10m windows > 5 events.
Sofia L.: postmortem checklist: - rollback applied ✅ - short-term iam patch applied ✅ - binder PR opened (#3421) - follow-up: add audit rule, add unit-tests for region label absence, and update runbook with rollback commands.
Maria G.: assigning owners: Jamal = short-term IAM patch & alert tuning, Patrick = binder PR & tests, Sofia = incident doc + follow-up with compliance for cross-region KMS policy.
Elaine (oncall): closing thread here, will update incident channel after monitoring for 30m. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: rollback completed on staging keystore-scope v1. logs: `release/keystore v1 rolled back at 1768888380`
